'''Cheon Jinwoo''' is a South Korean chemist and nanomedicine researcher. He is the H. G. Underwood Professor of Chemistry at [[Yonsei University]], the founding director of the [https://ibs.yonsei.ac.kr Center for Nanomedicine at the Institute for Basic Science (IBS)], and the director of the [https://maxplanck-yonsei-ibs.com Max Planck–Yonsei IBS Center for Nanomedicine Deep Tissue Control (MPYIC)]. 

Cheon is recognized for his contributions to inorganic materials chemistry and nanomedicine. His research focuses on developing chemical principles for the synthesis of inorganic nanoparticles and nanoprobes, and on their application to imaging, sensing, and controlling cellular functions in deep tissues of living systems.

Cheon is a fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]], the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], and the Korean Academy of Science and Technology. He serves as an associate editor of the ''Journal of the American Chemical Society(JACS)''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Journal of the American Chemical Society Editorial Board – ACS Publications |url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/jacsat/editors.html |access-date=2026-02-02 |website=pubs.acs.org |language=en |archive-date=2025-01-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250111213431/https://pubs.acs.org/page/jacsat/editors.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and previously served as a senior editor of ''Accounts of Chemical Research(ACR)''. He is also a member of the editorial advisory boards of several leading scientific journals, including C&EN.

Throughout his career, he has received numerous awards, including the [[Inchon Award]], the [[POSCO TJ Park Prize]]<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2013-01-31 |title=Alzheimer Research Award: B. Schmidt / TJ Park Science Award: J. Cheon / Imbach–Townsend Award: F. Seela / HMLS Investigator Award: C. Schultz |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1002/anie.201210065 |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |language=en |volume=52 |issue=8 |pages=2157 |doi=10.1002/anie.201210065 |bibcode=2013ACIE...52.2157. |issn=1433-7851 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702064306/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1002/anie.201210065 |archive-date=2019-07-02 |access-date=2019-07-02 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref>, and the [[Ho-Am Prize in Science]]. He has also been named a [[Clarivate Analytics]] [[Highly Cited Researchers|Highly Cited Researcher]] and received the [[Glenn T. Seaborg]] Memorial Lectureship in Chemistry.

==Education==
Cheon began his academic studies in chemistry at [[Yonsei University]] in 1981, where he earned his Bachelor of Science and [[Master of Science]] degrees in 1985 and 1987, respectively. He received his Ph.D. in chemistry in 1993 from the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] under the supervision of Professor [[Gregory S. Girolami]].

==Career and Research==
After completing his doctoral studies, Cheon conducted postdoctoral research at the [[University of California, Berkeley|UC Berkeley]], and worked as a research associate at the [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]]. He later returned to South Korea, where he joined the [[KAIST]], serving as an assistant and then associate professor.

In 2002, he joined Yonsei University as a faculty member and later became the H. G. Underwood Professor of Chemistry. From 2010 to 2016, he served as the director of the National Creative Research Initiative Center for Evolutionary Nanoparticles. In 2015, he became the founding director of the [[Institute for Basic Science|IBS]] Center for Nanomedicine at Yonsei University. In 2025, he co-founded Asia’s second Max Planck Center, the [https://maxplanck-yonsei-ibs.com Max Planck–Yonsei IBS Center for Nanomedicine Deep Tissue Control], serving as co-director alongside Professor Joachim Spatz of the [[Max Planck Institute for Medical Research]].

Cheon’s research has contributed to the development of nanomaterial-based biomedical technologies, including highly sensitive magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast agents<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jang |first1=Jung-tak |last2=Nah |first2=Hyunsoo |last3=Lee |first3=Jae-Hyun |last4=Moon |first4=Seung Ho |last5=Kim |first5=Min Gyu |last6=Cheon |first6=Jinwoo |date=2009-01-26 |title=Critical Enhancements of MRI Contrast and Hyperthermic Effects by Dopant-Controlled Magnetic Nanoparticles |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1002/ange.200805149 |journal=Angewandte Chemie |language=de |volume=121 |issue=7 |pages=1260–1264 |doi=10.1002/ange.200805149 |bibcode=2009AngCh.121.1260J |issn=0044-8249 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200729162026/https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1002/ange.200805149 |archive-date=2020-07-29 |access-date=2020-04-06 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=HyunShinEtAl>{{Cite journal |last1=Shin |first1=Tae-Hyun |last2=Choi |first2=Jin-sil |last3=Yun |first3=Seokhwan |last4=Kim |first4=Il-Sun |last5=Song |first5=Ho-Taek |last6=Kim |first6=Youngmee |last7=Park |first7=Kook In |last8=Cheon |first8=Jinwoo |title=''T'' <sub>1</sub> and ''T'' <sub>2</sub> Dual-Mode MRI Contrast Agent for Enhancing Accuracy by Engineered Nanomaterials |journal=ACS Nano |date=2014 |volume=8 |issue=4 |pages=3393–3401 |doi=10.1021/nn405977t |pmid=24673493 |bibcode=2014ACSNa...8.3393S }}</ref><ref>{{Cite patent|number=US20160000942A1|title=Mri contrast agent including t1 contrast material coated on surface of nanoparticle support|gdate=2016-01-07|invent1=Cheon|invent2=SHIN|inventor1-first=Jin Woo|inventor2-first=Tae Hyun|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US20160000942A1/en}} {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190704061022/https://patents.google.com/patent/US20160000942A1/en |date=2019-07-04 }}</ref> and nanoscale toolkits for cellular manipulation. In 2004, he experimentally demonstrated size-dependent MRI contrast effects using nanoparticles, which led to the development of magnetism-engineered iron oxide nanoparticles as ultra-sensitive MRI contrast agents with potential applications in early cancer detection.<ref name=HyunShinEtAl /><ref>{{Cite journal |date=2007-02-16 |title=Hot off the Press |url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2007/mb/b701393k |journal=Molecular BioSystems |language=en |volume=3 |issue=3 |pages=169–171 |doi=10.1039/B701393K |issn=1742-2051 |archive-date=2025-04-17 |access-date=2026-02-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250417110931/https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2007/mb/b701393k |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

He has also developed magnetic nanomachines composed of mechanically functional components at the submicrometer scale, enabling remote and precise control of nanostructures using external magnetic fields<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lin |first1=Mouhong |last2=Lee |first2=Jung-uk |last3=Kim |first3=Youngjoo |last4=Kim |first4=Gooreum |last5=Jung |first5=Yunmin |last6=Jo |first6=Ala |last7=Park |first7=Mansoo |last8=Lee |first8=Sol |last9=Lah |first9=Jungsu David |last10=Park |first10=Jongseong |last11=Noh |first11=Kunwoo |last12=Lee |first12=Jae-Hyun |last13=Kwak |first13=Minsuk |last14=Lungerich |first14=Dominik |last15=Cheon |first15=Jinwoo |date=May 2024 |title=A magnetically powered nanomachine with a DNA clutch |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41565-023-01599-6 |journal=Nature Nanotechnology |language=en |volume=19 |issue=5 |pages=646–651 |doi=10.1038/s41565-023-01599-6 |pmid=38326466 |bibcode=2024NatNa..19..646L |issn=1748-3395 |archive-date=2024-12-10 |access-date=2024-12-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241210071021/https://www.nature.com/articles/s41565-023-01599-6 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref>. These systems have been explored for applications such as targeted drug delivery and minimally invasive therapeutic approaches.

Since 2021, Cheon’s work has significantly advanced the field of [[magnetogenetics]], particularly for wireless control of deep tissue and brain activity in vivo<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lee |first1=Jung-uk |last2=Shin |first2=Wookjin |last3=Lim |first3=Yongjun |last4=Kim |first4=Jungsil |last5=Kim |first5=Woon Ryoung |last6=Kim |first6=Heehun |last7=Lee |first7=Jae-Hyun |last8=Cheon |first8=Jinwoo |date=July 2021 |title=Non-contact long-range magnetic stimulation of mechanosensitive ion channels in freely moving animals |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41563-020-00896-y |journal=Nature Materials |language=en |volume=20 |issue=7 |pages=1029–1036 |doi=10.1038/s41563-020-00896-y |pmid=33510447 |bibcode=2021NatMa..20.1029L |issn=1476-4660 |archive-date=2024-12-10 |access-date=2024-12-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241210071021/https://www.nature.com/articles/s41563-020-00896-y |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Choi |first1=Seo-Hyun |last2=Shin |first2=Jihye |last3=Park |first3=Chanhyun |last4=Lee |first4=Jung-uk |last5=Lee |first5=Jaegyeong |last6=Ambo |first6=Yuko |last7=Shin |first7=Wookjin |last8=Yu |first8=Ri |last9=Kim |first9=Ju-Young |last10=Lah |first10=Jungsu David |last11=Shin |first11=Donghun |last12=Kim |first12=Gooreum |last13=Noh |first13=Kunwoo |last14=Koh |first14=Wuhyun |last15=Lee |first15=C. Justin |date=September 2024 |title=In vivo magnetogenetics for cell-type-specific targeting and modulation of brain circuits |url=https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-3889996/latest.pdf |journal=Nature Nanotechnology |language=en |volume=19 |issue=9 |pages=1333–1343 |doi=10.1038/s41565-024-01694-2 |pmid=38956320 |bibcode=2024NatNa..19.1333C |issn=1748-3395|url-access= }}</ref>. Magnetogenetics employs magnetic nanoparticles to generate mechanical forces or torque that activate mechanosensitive ion channels, such as [[PIEZO1|Piezo1]], enabling non-invasive and long-distance modulation of neuronal circuits. This approach offers new tools for studying brain function and has potential implications for the treatment of neurological disorders.
